title: Stereomicroscopy and 3D-target myeloperoxidase intestinal phenotyping following a fecal flora homogenization protocol
protocol: Get 6 mice from each colony, one mouse per cage if possible.
Collect one fecal pellet per mouse.
Ensure an equal number of male and female mice are collected from each colony.
Identify the corner where mice piled their excrements in each cage.
Collect approximately 200 g of full thickness soiled bedding material from each source cage.
Pool all collected cage bedding material into one empty autoclaved cage.
Mix the pooled beddings with sterile PBS to create a thick fecal slurry.
Take samples to the laboratory for preparation of the fecal inoculum.
Place all pellets in a 15 mL tube containing 9-10 mL of PBS and about 500 mg of ceramica or glass beads.
Vortex the tube vigorously to break down the pellets and homogenize the mixture.
Spin the tube at 500-1000 g for 5 seconds to decant heavy particles.
Transfer the supernatant using a syringe and a gavage needle into a new tube.
Prepare the bedding inoculum by pooling all bedding material.
Soak the pooled bedding material with PBS.
Massage the soaked bedding manually while wearing two pairs of gloves to create a slurry.
Hand squeeze the bedding and collect the liquid in 15 mL tubes.
Load 10 mL of slurry into each tube for freezing at -80°C if storage is desired.
Spin the pooled bedding suspension for 500-1000 g for 5 or 10 seconds.
Transfer the supernatant using a syringe and a gavage needle to a new tube.
Place approximately 200 g of homogenized soaked bedding material in each cage.
Administer via gavage 200-400 μL of a combination of bedding:feces (1:1, v/v) supernatants/suspensions to each mouse on day one.
Fast the mice for 3-6 hours if 400 μL of suspension are to be gavaged.
Consult your IACUC veterinarian for autoclaving protocols of approved rodent diets.
Use double-irradiated vacuum and sterile packed diets if preferred.
Autoclave specially balanced laboratory autoclavable rodent diets at 121°C for 30-45 minutes, in food layers of <3 inches thick.
Follow manufacturer’s instructions for autoclaving specially balanced laboratory autoclavable rodent diets.
Replace the bedding and gavage the mice again on day 2.
Replace the bedding and gavage the mice again on day 3.
Monitor the mice for an additional 4 days, changing the bedding once daily.
Collect fecal samples for 16S analysis if desired to assess microbiome similarity or divergence.
Start phenotyping experiments, such as response to DSS-administration in the drinking water.
Consider different waiting periods depending on the study objective.
Alternatively, conduct IsPreFeH two days after oral antibiotic treatment using a non-absorbable antimicrobial agent like streptomycin (20 mg/kg).
Validate each approach for each case scenario.
Dissect tissues according to architecture.
Mix 3.48 g of potassium phosphate dibasic trihydrate with 400 mL ddH₂O for solution A.
Dissolve 0.87 g of potassium phosphate monobasic in 100 mL ddH₂O for solution B.
Add solution B to solution A gradually to adjust the pH to 6.0.
Store the prepared PPB buffer at room temperature, protected from light, for up to two months.
Prepare fresh batches of PPB buffer the day prior to testing.
Dissolve 0.5g of HTAB with 100mL of working pH-6.0-adjusted Potassium Phosphate Buffer.
Place the solution in a heat stirring plate set to 50°C with a stirring magnet.
Prepare fresh HTBA buffer prior to testing and keep cool, below room temperature.
Dissolve 20 μL of 30% H₂O₂ into 580 μL of ddH₂O in a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube.
Protect the hydrogen peroxide solution from light with aluminum foil.
Keep the hydrogen peroxide solution cool by placing it on crushed ice (~4°C).
Prepare fresh hydrogen peroxide solution prior to use.
Dissolve a 10 mg tablet of o-Dianisidine dihydrochloride in a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 45 mL ddH₂O and 5 mL potassium phosphate buffer to the dissolved tablet.
Cover the solution with foil to protect from light.
Mix well using a vortex mixer.
Prepare this substrate right before MPO testing with freshly prepared homogenates.
Supplement each 10 mL of Dianisidine substrate with 10 μL of 1% H₂O₂ for every 10 samples.
Add the supplemented solution to each well immediately after preparation.
Euthanize animals as approved by your IACUC regulations.
Collect fresh tissues in 1.7 mL microcentrifuge Eppendorf conical tubes.
Flash freeze collected tissues on liquid nitrogen or dry ice.
Use 2 mL Eppendorf flat-bottomed tubes if preferred, but use 1.7 mL conical tubes for very small samples less than 10 mg.
Do not process more than 50 mg of tissue.
Prepare 1 mL of lysis buffer for each sample exceeding the limit.
Homogenize tissues in Lysis buffer.
Concentrate tissue debris using the cone shape of the Eppendorf conical tubes.
Pipette 10 μL of homogenized supernatant for testing.
Store samples at -80°C until ready for the MPO Assay.
Avoid thawing samples on crushed ice.
Keep samples frozen at -80°C until measuring weight.
Cover Eppendorf tubes fully with dry ice to prevent exposure to room temperature.
Process frozen samples in batches of up to 24 samples.
Ensure samples remain frozen until a few minutes prior to testing.
Follow strict sample refrigeration after thawing/homogenization to prevent inadvertent MPO activity at room temperature.
Prepare scale, dry ice tray and setting to handle and cut frozen tissues.
Place the forceps and scalpels standing on dry ice.
Keep plastic boats and Eppendorf tube lids frozen for rapid handling of frozen tissues.
Take tissues/samples from deep freezer and put on dry ice. Cover completely.
Cut a piece of frozen sample ~15-25 mg (up to 50 mg per homogenizing session).
Perform the procedure while keeping samples frozen until immediately before adding HTBA Lysis buffer.
Add HTBA buffer to the sample and place the mixture back on ice for prompt homogenization.
Weigh tissue.
Place tissue inside an Eppendorf tube with glass beads.
Mix tissue with glass beads.
Add HTBA buffer to the tissue-containing tube at a rate of 50 mg per mL with HTAB lysis buffer for homogenization.
Balance tubes in homogenizer.
Run homogenizing session in walk-in refrigerated room (4°C) if possible for 60 seconds with rapid oscillations at 4 m/s.
Alternatively, use deep cold-resistant holders if samples need to be kept frozen (<20°C).
Or homogenize in runs of 20-30 second intervals and place samples on ice for 3-5 minutes between cycles.
Process comparable amounts of tissues across all samples (average 15 mg, range 10-25 mg).
Cut samples into smaller pieces if they are denser or larger.
Homogenize the samples until frothy and free of visible tissue chunks.
Centrifuge the homogenized samples at 4°C for 5 minutes at 12,500 rpm.
Keep the supernatant refrigerated without disrupting the debris-supernatant interface.
Chill an ELISA plate on crushed ice.
Mix Dianisidine substrate by combining 90 mL ddH₂O, 10 mL potassium phosphate buffer, and 1 Dianisidine tablet.
Vortex the Dianisidine mixture thoroughly and cover with foil to protect from light.
Keep the Dianisidine mixture at room temperature until just before use.
Load 10 μL of sample supernatant into each of three wells (triplicates) on a pre-chilled 96-well flat-bottom ELISA plate.
Start loading samples in rows A1, A2, and A3 for the first sample, then B1, B2, and B3 for the second sample.
Leave column 4 empty to prevent pipetting mistakes.
Resume loading sample 9 from wells A5, A6, and A7, sample 10 from wells B5, B6, and B7.
Leave column 8 empty.
Finish with samples 17 through 24 in the final rows H10, H11, and H12.
If a blank is desired to ensure no background colorimetric reactions occur, use 10 μL of HTAB lysis buffer instead of tissue supernatant for the blank.
Add 200 μL of active dianisidine substrate to each sample well using an 8-channel pipette.
Start with column 1 and follow the order 5, 9, 2, 6, 10, 3, 7, and 11 for distribution.
Immediately read the plate at A450 absorbance.
Measure OD<sub>450</sub> changes using plate reader spectrophotometer every 30 seconds for 5 minutes at 28°C.
Use 28°C as the temperature to estimate enzymatic activity.
Calculate MPO activity using an excel file for more reproducible results.
Estimate MPO by averaging triplicate results for three time points.
Find the difference in absorbance (ΔA450(t30-t0)) from time 0s to 30s.
Determine the difference (ΔA450(t60-t30)) from time 30s to 60s.
Average these two ΔA450 values for the final change.
Use example output from the plate reader.
Open and use the excel template file with our calculations available in the Supplementary Excel file.
